newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down on slack demand, crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down on slack demand, crude.

text.p: Both light distillates were softer on Tuesday with crude and slack demand although Taiwan's May naphtha import tender award was higher than the previous month, traders said.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender 28,000 tonnes of naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha for delivery May 11-31 at just below $230 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung, a company official said.
The award was higher than CPC's last purchase of N+A in early March for April 16-30 delivery was at $210-$215 per tonne c-and-f.
The official explained the higher award on the low interest in the tender which only received four offers when it closed March 24.
April naphtha swaps fell by 50 cents per barrel to $23.05/$23.25.
"It is down pretty much in line with crude but buying the naphtha crack now is good,' said one trader.
Sentiment has weakened because of talk of arbitrage cargoes. A Swiss trader was heard loading a 60,000-tonne cargo from Skikda in early April for May arrival in Asia, a trader said.

Gasoline edged down slightly in a well-offered market with two 50,000-barrel lots of unleaded 97-octane was traded at $28.55 per barrel fob Singapore lifting April 8-11 and 10-15, between a U.S. major and a shosha, and a European major and a Dutch trader respectively.
Both unleaded 92- and 95-octane April fob cargoes were offered at $28.00 and $28.10 respectively. On Monday, 92-octane was offered at $28.00 and 95-octane at $28.65.
The only regional demand was from Vietnam, but for low octane 83-octane leaded grade, which is not often traded. The tender closes Friday and is valid for a week.
